summary: The school district emphasizes the critical role of E-Rate in maintaining essential network infrastructure for modern education, citing the direct impact of reduced E-Rate support on their budget and operational needs. The school district argues against sunsetting the E-Rate program, emphasizing its importance for maintaining reliable broadband infrastructure and connectivity for students. The school urges the FCC to preserve and improve the program rather than eliminate it.

claims.argument: Reducing E-Rate would increase budgetary strain on school districts
claims.evidence_quote: Rock Hill School District 3 has received $2.13 million in committed federal E-Rate support over funding years 2021–2025 — an average of roughly $425,602 a year toward the connections our students depend on. That support does not represent a one-time build; it is the recurring cost of keeping a modern network running.

claims.argument: A rural-only rule would overlook the needs of students in a district like ours simply because a school falls on the other side of a geographic line. E-Rate’s success over the past three decades should be viewed as a reason to preserve and improve the program — not as a reason to assume that the work is finished.
